text:
sre-bot: ALERT: SLO burn-rate detected for route /api/generate. Multi-window trigger: 3-window burn=4.2x (1m/5m/15m). Pager triggered.
pagerduty: Pager: oncall=mike. Severity: P2. Incident link: https://redwood/incident/INC-2026-512
mike: Acknowledged — taking the pager. Pulling traces and recent deploys. Any deploys in last 30m?
anya: No deploys from product in that window. Canary metrics show spike starting ~2479123220.
mike: Seeing p95 latency jump to ~1.6s (baseline ~200ms) and 5xx rate ~1.8%. Traces point to increased KV cache misses on gpu-node-12.
tara: I see GC pause spikes and elevated mem churn on node-12 around 2479123205. Might be evicting KV slices.
chris: For quick mitigation: can we route traffic off node-12 and reduce consumer concurrency? That should lower tail latency and error amplification.
mike: Routing rule updated — excluding node-12 now (rolled 100% in 2m). Error rate is trending down. Applying a temporary node-specific mute to reduce alert noise.
sre-bot: Note: Temporary mute applied for alerts tied to gpu-node-12 for 60m (inc-channel).
anya: Thinking about follow-ups: current SLO burn alert is very sensitive to short infra blips. Proposal: move multi-window config for /api/generate from [1m,5m,15m] to [5m,15m,60m] and add a small min_budget floor (e.g., 0.02) so tiny bursts don't page. Also require >=2 windows breaching before paging.
mike: I don't want global policy changes mid-incident. Let's validate in staging first. Example quick rule to test in staging:
```
alert_rule:
  name: slo_burn_route_generate
  windows: [5m,15m,60m]
  burn_thresholds: [3.0,2.0,1.5]
  min_budget: 0.02
  page_if: ">=2 windows breaching"
```
tara: +1 on a staging run. Also strongly want a dashboard panel showing node-level KV miss rate and GC pause histogram to catch this class of failure earlier.
anya: Action items: (1) chris — run the multi-window rule test in staging and post results; (2) tara — add dashboard panels (KV miss rate, GC pauses, per-node error heatmap); (3) mike — file postmortem draft and include a customer-impact estimate; (4) ops — schedule a 1h tuning review to decide policy changes.
chris: Starting the staging run now, will paste results.
mike: Quick customer-impact summary: ~12 failed requests observed in the spike window (~10 minutes), degraded latency for ~3% of traffic. No escalations received yet. Will quantify in postmortem.
sre-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: SLO burn back to normal ranges. Summary: transient KV cache eviction due to GC spike on gpu-node-12; routing work-around and temporary mute applied. Resolution doc: https://redwood/incident/INC-2026-512/resolve
mike: Thanks everyone for the fast triage. We'll reconvene in the tuning review to land any conservative changes. :thumbsup:
